invariant: PlantUML Entity and Link constructors consume one shared CucaDiagram.cpt1 sequence at the instant each object is created. Commands may interleave object kinds on the same source line. In particular, CommandCreateClass creates the child, then manageExtends creates one missing parent and its Link before moving to the next missing parent and Link. Association construction consumes the apoint short name, point Entity, and three replacement Links; it consumes one additional temporary A-B Link only when foundLink returns null. When foundLink returns an existing base Link, createNew removes that Link and reuses its type, labels, length, and endpoint order without constructing the temporary Link. The resulting graph and public SVEK IDs reflect these constructor and replacement events, not a later sort by source line or object category.
causal_divergence: Rust stores entities, relationships, packages, notes, and association classes in separate vectors and originally reconstructed the shared counter using CucaUidEvent.sort_key, which could not recover arbitrary same-line constructor interleaving. The typed event replay fixes that class of error, but Association events still hardcode six slots and the parser leaves a preexisting A-B relationship in the rendered relationship vector. Java's existing-link branch consumes five slots and replaces that base relationship with the association point's split links. The no-base control therefore passes while a preexisting-base case retains one extra Rust link and shifts every subsequent UID by one.
planned_change: Continue recording typed UID creation events at parser materialization time. When parsing an association class, identify the same preexisting A-B relationship that Java foundLink would select, record on AssociationClass whether a base Link was replaced, and exclude that relationship from ordinary SVEK rendering without erasing its already-consumed UID event. Replay an Association event as five slots for the replacement branch and six for the no-base branch. Retain deterministic reconstruction only for manually constructed diagrams and older serialized models, deriving the branch from surviving relationship state where possible. Do not key behavior to labels, fixture names, coordinates, or fixed corpus topology.
